title: All-quotient coherence of the canonical finite evaluation of tower pullback
statement:
Let $g:T'\to T$ and $A,I,P_n=A/I^n,A_T,A_{T'}$ satisfy [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Use its strict reduction functor $\mathcal R_T$ and the canonical universal tower pullback $\widetilde L_0$ of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Let $B_n(K)=Lg_n^*(K\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T)$, regarded as an $A_{T'}$-complex by the finite projection, and let
$$F_{0,n}:\operatorname{ev}'_n\widetilde L_0\mathcal R_T(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}B_n(K)$$
be the canonical finite coefficient comparison induced by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. Write $d_{0,b,a}$ for the actual strict tower transition and $d_{B,b,a}$ for the finite target quotient map using the canonical restriction-of-scalars composition identification. For every $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$ and $b\geq a\geq1$,
$$d_{B,b,a}F_{0,b}=F_{0,a}d_{0,b,a}.$$
The finite target normalization uses $(x\otimes r)\otimes s\mapsto x\otimes q_{b,a}(r)s$; these identifications satisfy the equal-index identity and the three-index quotient cocycle.

proof.text: Put $R=\underline A_T$, $R'=\underline A_{T'}$, $B=A_T$, $B'=A_{T'}$, and $S_n=(P_n)_T$, $S_n'=(P_n)_{T'}$. The finite coefficient structure theorem identifies each $S_n$ with the constant ring sheaf, preserving constant sections. The constant-completion comparison gives flat $R\to B$, $R'\to B'$ and the projection-normalized identifications $B/I^nB=S_n$, $B'/I^nB'=S_n'$. Write $G=g_B^*$ for completed-coefficient module pullback and $g_R^*$ for constant-$A$ module inverse image. Choose a flat-term K-flat representative $P\to K$. In the category of strict towers of $R$-module complexes, choose one objectwise flat-term K-flat resolution $v:V_\bullet\to(S_n[0])_n$. This uses the small category $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$, not separately chosen resolutions with unrelated transition maps. Write $t_{b,a}:V_b\to V_a$ for its arrows, so $v_at_{b,a}=q_{b,a}v_b$ for every $b\geq a$.

proof.text: Define $H_n=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R V_n)$, with arrows $1\otimes t_{b,a}$. Balancing identifies this with $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_B(B\otimes_R V_n))$. Extension of scalars makes $B\otimes_R V_n$ K-flat over $B$ with flat terms, and the total-tensor lemma makes $H_n$ K-flat over $B$ with flat terms. The balancing map is $x\otimes(b\otimes z)\mapsto bx\otimes z$, with inverse $x\otimes z\mapsto x\otimes(1\otimes z)$; it commutes with the differentials and the maps $t_{b,a}$. Thus $H_\bullet$ is in the resolving class used for the universal tower pullback.

proof.text: Let $R(P)_n=P\otimes_B S_n$. Restriction makes $P$ K-flat over $R$, since $B$ is flat over $R$. Consequently $1\otimes v_n:P\otimes_R V_n\to P\otimes_R S_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism: its cone is the tensor of $P$ with the acyclic cone of $v_n$. The common-quotient comparison identifies $P\otimes_R S_n$ with $P\otimes_B S_n$, using the ordinary projection-normalized quotient maps. Their composites give $r_n:H_n\to R(P)_n$. Since $v_at_{b,a}=q_{b,a}v_b$, these maps form a quasi-isomorphism $r:H_\bullet\to R(P)_\bullet$ of strict $B$-tower complexes, with $R(P)$ representing $\mathcal R_T(K)$.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 07A2 (lemma-tensor-product-K-flat), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change); simultaneous coefficient-resolution argument below, written by Q34

proof.text:
Set $D_n=g_n^*(P\otimes_B S_n)$, regarded as a $B'$-complex. The finite coefficient structure maps $c_{g,n}$ are isomorphisms by the constant-ring structure theorem. The ordinary balancing comparison
$$\beta_n:G(P\otimes_B S_n)\longrightarrow D_n$$
is an isomorphism: both sides identify with $g^{-1}P\otimes_{g^{-1}B}S_n'$. On pure sections it sends $(g^{-1}x\otimes g^{-1}s)\otimes b'$ to $g^{-1}x\otimes c_{g,n}(g^{-1}s)\pi_n'(b')$, in that common tensor presentation; its inverse sends $g^{-1}x\otimes s'$ to $(g^{-1}x\otimes c_{g,n}^{-1}(s'))\otimes1$. Here the projection square $\pi_n'c_g=c_{g,n}g^{-1}\pi_n$ makes the balancing relations identical. For $b\geq a$, the finite constant-map identity $q_{b,a}'c_{g,b}=c_{g,a}g^{-1}q_{b,a}$ shows that the two composites from $G(R(P)_b)$ to $D_a$ have this same formula with $q_{b,a}'$ applied to the scalar. Therefore the $\beta_n$ form a strict $B'$-tower isomorphism, with target arrows induced by $g^{-1}(1\otimes q_{b,a})$ and the canonical restriction-of-scalars identifications.

proof.text:
We must check that $\alpha_n=\beta_nG(r_n):G(H_n)\to D_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism; $R(P)_n$ need not be K-flat over $B$. The natural cochain pullback/tensor comparison, followed by balancing scalar extension, identifies
$$G(H_n)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(G(P)\otimes_{R'}g_R^*V_n),\qquad
D_n\cong G(P)\otimes_{B'}S_n'\cong G(P)\otimes_{R'}S_n'.$$
Under these identifications $\alpha_n$ is $1\otimes g_R^*v_n$. To check its normalization, send a pure section $(g^{-1}(x\otimes z))\otimes b'$ to $(g^{-1}x\otimes b')\otimes g^{-1}z$ before augmentation; either composite gives $g^{-1}x\otimes\pi_n'(b')c_{g,n}(g^{-1}v_n(z))$. The inverse balancing inserts $1$ in the extra scalar factor. Naturality of the cochain comparison ensures these are maps of complexes, also for unbounded direct-sum total tensors.

proof.text: Pullback preserves K-flatness and flat terms, so $G(P)$ is flat-term K-flat over $B'$. Since $B'$ is flat over $R'$, its restriction is K-flat over $R'$. The constant-ring inverse-image theorem applies to the arbitrary ring $A$, and says that $g_R^*$ is exact; hence $g_R^*v_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism with target $S_n'$. Tensoring its acyclic cone with the restricted $G(P)$ is acyclic. By the computation in Step 5, each $\alpha_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Step 4 and strictness of $r$ show that $\alpha:G(H_\bullet)\to D_\bullet$ is a morphism of strict $B'$-tower complexes.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 07A2 (lemma-tensor-product-K-flat), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change); simultaneous coefficient-resolution argument below, written by Q34

proof.text:
Write $Q_{\rm Tow},Q'_{\rm Tow}$ for tower localization and $\tau$ for the universal derived counit. The resolving-class computation gives the tower isomorphism
$$\chi=\tau_{H_\bullet}\,\widetilde L_0(Q_{\rm Tow}r)^{-1}:
\widetilde L_0\mathcal R_T(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q'_{\rm Tow}G(H_\bullet).$$
Compose it with $Q'_{\rm Tow}(\alpha)$. At level $n$ this is the canonical $F_{0,n}$: exact finite inverse image identifies $D_n$ with $B_n(K)$; the comparisons in Steps 3 and 5 are the ordinary common-quotient and scalar-insertion comparisons that induce the stated constant-completion comparison. In particular the map is induced by the fixed projection $B'\to S_n'$ and by $c_{g,n}$. The evaluation-normalization lemma identifies evaluation of $\chi$ with the inverse of $L_0(r_n)$ followed by the level derived counit, so this is also the prescribed finite comparison for the universal evaluation construction. The resolving-class comparison is natural under quasi-isomorphisms between resolving models, so this identification is independent of $P$ and $V_\bullet$.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 07A2 (lemma-tensor-product-K-flat), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change); simultaneous coefficient-resolution argument below, written by Q34

proof.text:
Every arrow of $Q'_{\rm Tow}(\alpha)\chi$ is a morphism in the derived category of strict towers. Its evaluations therefore commute with every transition: for $b\geq a$, strictness of $\chi$ gives $G(t^H_{b,a})\chi_b=\chi_a d_{0,b,a}$, and strictness of $\alpha$ gives $d_{D,b,a}\alpha_b=\alpha_aG(t^H_{b,a})$. Composing yields
$$d_{B,b,a}F_{0,b}=d_{D,b,a}\alpha_b\chi_b
=\alpha_aG(t^H_{b,a})\chi_b
=\alpha_a\chi_a d_{0,b,a}=F_{0,a}d_{0,b,a}.$$
Here $t^H_{b,a}=1\otimes t_{b,a}$ and the chain maps are understood after localization. Step 4 identifies $d_D$ with the specified finite quotient map $d_B$ on the underlying $B'$-complexes.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 07A2 (lemma-tensor-product-K-flat), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change); simultaneous coefficient-resolution argument below, written by Q34

proof.text:
Finally $P\otimes_BS_b$ is a flat-term K-flat $S_b$-complex by K-flat change of rings; finite inverse image carries it to a flat-term K-flat $S_b'$-complex. Thus $D_b$ computes $B_b(K)$ with its finite coefficient action. Successive derived scalar extension is represented by the ordinary balancing map
$$(x\otimes r)\otimes s\longmapsto x\otimes q_{b,a}'(r)s,$$
with inverse $x\otimes s\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes s$. Pullback of this map has the same formula because the finite constant coefficient maps commute with $q_{b,a}$. It is therefore the normalization used in Step 4, including its restriction-of-scalars composition identification. For $b=a$ the formula is scalar multiplication and hence the unit identification. For $c\geq b\geq a$, both reassociations send $((x\otimes r_c)\otimes r_b)\otimes r_a$ to $x\otimes q_{c,a}'(r_c)q_{b,a}'(r_b)r_a$. Equality on pure sections determines the sheaf tensor maps, so these are the equal-index identity and three-index quotient cocycle in the finite derived categories.
